system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.

answer.title: Answer

output.answer:
Okay, I need to finish the bar graph based on the table. Let's see... how many cars were 'Slow'? I count 10 'X's under 'Slow'. So I need to make the bar for 'Slow' go all the way up to the '10' on the vertical axis. Right now, it's only at 9. I will draw the bar taller, so that the top of the bar touches the '10' mark. 

Now, let's look at 'Medium'. There are 8 'X's under 'Medium'. So I will draw a bar in the 'Medium' column that goes all the way up to the '8' mark on the vertical axis. It should be the same width as the 'Slow' bar. 

Finally, let's look at 'Fast'. There are 6 'X's under 'Fast'. I'll draw a bar in the 'Fast' column that goes all the way up to the '6' mark on the vertical axis. It should also be the same width as the other bars. 

So, to describe what I would draw, I would make a bar in the 'Medium' column reaching the '8' mark on the vertical axis and a bar in the 'Fast' column reaching the '6' mark on the vertical axis. All three bars should be the same width.
